chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Imam delivers the sermon on Friday, it is not appropriate for anyone to speak until the Imam finishes his sermon. When the Imam finishes his sermon, one may speak between that and the establishment of the prayer. Whether he hears the recitation or not, it suffices for him.

key_terms.تُقَامَ اَلصَّلَاةَ: The establishment of the prayer (standing for it)
key_terms.خُطْبَتِهِ: The sermon delivered by the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during the Friday sermon and after it until the prayer begins?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential ruling that the Friday sermon (khutbah) must be delivered in silence by the congregation, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition of reverence. It clarifies that the validity of the congregational prayer is not contingent upon hearing the Imam's Quranic recitation, emphasizing the structural integrity of the khutbah as a prerequisite for the prayer itself.
